The approach featurizes molecules using ECFP6 fingerprints of size 500, which is the maximum numberof features tested by TabPFN. The training data is fit with a TabPFNRegressor, which is a pretrainedtabular foundation model. It uses in-context learning to adapt to the ADMET dataset and makepredictions on the test set. This is an entirely black box approach that treats the ADMET data asan arbitrary tabular dataset. Further details are in writeup.md in the GitHub repository, which isarchived on Zenodo.

Multitask deep ordinal regression model

Datasets from diverse sources (incl. ChEMBL, OChem, Deepchem, ADMET-AI, TDC, biogen and DrugBank) were used to prepare consolidated datasets for each ADMET endpoint of interest. A non-redundant feature space from the SMILES was prepared using mordred applied on an antivirals library. Consensus with Chemprop enabled us to identify 55 features. Both the raw SMILES as well as the feature spaces were used to train Graph NNs and Boosting models respectively. Post hyperparameter optimization via cross-validation and independent test set evaluation, the best model for each problem was identified. This model was rebuilt on the respective full dataset and applied on the Polaris-admet-2025 test set, for each of the problems.
